title: Prior work: four groups of methods
hints: 4 groups: assignment / route guidance / planners (deadlocks & collisions) / jam handling
Each fixes one kind of congestion locally
None avoids congestion at assignment level, whole system
Our question: a global scheduling algorithm?
en: 【依次指四张卡】 Earlier methods fall into four groups. **Order assignment** gives robots close, cheap orders. **Route guidance** makes busy roads cost more, so robots spread out. **Planners** decide which robot moves first, and avoid **deadlocks and collisions**. **Jam handling** keeps some robots idle, or sorts out robots that meet in a narrow passage. 【指底部黄框】 In all the methods we read, each one only fixes **one kind of congestion locally**. None starts from **the whole system** and weighs many factors to **avoid congestion when orders are given out**. {So we wanted to try:} is there a **global scheduling algorithm** that avoids congestion?
zh: 【依次指四张卡】前人的方法可以分成四类。**派单**给车分近的、便宜的单。**选路**让拥挤的路代价更高，把车分散开。**规划**决定哪台车先走，避免**死锁和碰撞**。**拥堵处理**让一部分车闲着，或者处理在窄道里碰上的车。【指底部黄框】在我们读到的所有方法里，每一种都只是**单独在局部优化某种拥塞**，没有一种从**整个系统**出发、同时考虑多个因素**在派单层面去避免拥塞**，所以我们想进行这个尝试，看看有没有一种**全局调度算法**去避免拥塞。

title: Why did changing routes not help?
figs: 图 4 地图压成网络（公式直接写在右边文字里）
hints: Model: 16 rooms = nodes, 31 doors = edges; door 6 is a cut
906 ÷ 3,614 ≈ 0.2507 (counted on the map)
Door 6 ≈ 26 / 500 ticks: counted in 5 runs, 1,175 crossings ÷ 45 periods (first 500 ticks left out) → 26 ÷ 0.376 ≈ 69
14 of 15 rerouting methods lowered results → the question is scheduling
en: {Thank you. So why did changing routes not help? First, we built a model.} 【指左图】 The **16 rooms are nodes** and the **31 doors are edges**; 【指红线门 6】 **door 6 is a cut**{: without it, the four lower-left rooms are cut off}. 【指右 1】 {Counted on the map,} the lower-left rooms hold **906 of the 3,614** room cells: **906 ÷ 3,614 ≈ 0.2507**{, a quarter}. 【指右 2】 {With random pickups and deliveries,} an order crosses door 6 when its two ends are on different sides: **2 × 0.2507 × 0.7493 ≈ 37.6 percent**; {counting} the task file gives 38.5. 【指公式】 Door 6 passes about **26 robots** per 500 ticks: {we counted crossings in 5 simulation runs,} **1,175 crossings ÷ 45 periods of 500 ticks ≈ 26**. {So} the map can finish at most **26 ÷ 0.376 ≈ 69 orders** per 500 ticks, **whatever the routes**. {That is why} **14 of 15** rerouting methods we tried lowered results. {The real question is} **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**: **scheduling**.
zh: 谢谢。那为什么改路线没有用？我们先建了一个模型。【指左图】**16 个房间是点，31 道门是线**；【指红线门 6】**门 6 是一个割**：没有它，左下 4 个房间就断开了。【指右 1】在地图上数格子：左下房间占 3614 个房间格里的 **906 个**，**906 ÷ 3614 ≈ 0.2507**，约四分之一。【指右 2】取货点和送货点随机落下时，一单两头在门的两侧才要过门 6，概率是 **2 × 0.2507 × 0.7493 ≈ 37.6%**；数任务文件得到 38.5%。【指公式】门 6 每 500 拍大约过 **26 台**：我们在 5 局仿真里数过门的车，**1175 次过门 ÷ 45 个 500 拍 ≈ 26**。所以**不管车怎么走**，整张图每 500 拍最多完成 **26 ÷ 0.376 ≈ 69 单**。所以我们试过的 15 种换路办法里有 **14 种**都变差。真正的问题是**派多少车、哪边先走**，也就是**调度**。

segs.en: {Thank you. So why did changing routes not help? First, we built a model.} 【指左图】 The **16 rooms are nodes** and the **31 doors are edges**; 【指红线门 6】 **door 6 is a cut**{: without it, the four lower-left rooms are cut off}.

title: What makes our robots different
figs: 对比表（我们的车 / 计算机网络 / 道路交通，幻灯片上直接画的，阴影 = 和我们的车不一样）
hints: vs networks: they drop packets; vs traffic: no car may wait forever; here one program decides
→ copy neither: we had to build our own new algorithm, DoorFlow
DoorFlow never drops a robot; decides who goes and when; keeps exits clear
en: 【指表格】 Our analysis also showed where we differ from **computer networks** and **road traffic**. A congested network can simply **drop packets**; a robot **cannot be dropped**, and a waiting robot **takes up a cell**. Road traffic cannot leave some cars **standing still forever**, but here we can. And **one program decides every order and move**, not each driver. {So} we **cannot simply copy** network or traffic algorithms; we had to come up with **a completely new algorithm of our own**: **DoorFlow**. {So} DoorFlow **never drops a robot**; it only decides **who goes and when**, and keeps **exits clear**.
zh: 【指表格】同时我们的分析发现了我们和计算机网络和交通流算法不一样的地方：计算机网络里拥塞往往可以直接**丢包**来解决，车**不能因为拥塞被丢弃**；而且等着的车**占着格子**；对于交通来说，交通不能让某些车辆**永远不动**，但是这里我们可以；而且这里**每一单、每一步都由一个程序统一决定**，不像路上每个司机自己选路。所以都**不能直接抄**和借用交通流和计算机网络的算法，我们必须想出**自己全新的算法**：**DoorFlow**。所以我们后来的方向转向了让**出口保持畅通**。

title: Scheduling 1: a quota for each door
figs: 名额大小原理图（从“路上的车数 = 过门速率 × 路程时间”推出；这条计数规律在排队论里叫 Little 定律，讲稿不提名字，只写在图注里；理论示意）
hints: Robots on the way to a door: hold an order through it, not crossed yet (counted live)
Door quota = the most robots allowed on the way at once → how many orders through the door at the same time
Door takes one robot every r ticks, trip T ticks → T ÷ r on the way → quota = door rate × trip time
Metro: a train every 2 min, trip 20 min → 20 ÷ 2 = 10 trains running at once
Fewer: door waits; more: queue, block the other side

segs.en: {How many robots should head for door 6 at once?} We came up with a way to **measure how many robots are on the way** to a door: robots that hold an order through it but have not crossed yet. We put a limit on this number, the **door quota**: it decides **how many orders may cross the door at the same time**.
segs.zh: 同时该有多少车奔向门 6？我们想到一个办法：**衡量在途、会通过某个门口的车有多少**，也就是接了要过这道门的单、还没过门的车。我们给这个数设一个上限，叫**门的名额**，用它来决定**同时指派多少个要穿过这道门的任务**。
key: **Robots on the way** to a door: hold an order through it, not crossed yet (**counted live**)
**Door quota**: the most robots allowed on the way at once → **how many orders through the door at the same time**

segs.en: {How big should the quota be?} If the door takes one robot every **r** ticks and a trip takes **T** ticks, keeping the door busy needs everything sent in the last T ticks on the way: **T ÷ r** robots. {So} **quota = door rate × trip time**.
segs.zh: 名额该多大？如果门每 **r** 拍放进一台，一趟路要 **T** 拍，要让门一直有车过，过去 T 拍里派出的车都得在路上，也就是 **T ÷ r** 台。所以**名额 = 过门速率 × 路程时间**。
key: How big? Door passes one robot every **r** ticks · a trip takes **T** ticks
Door never waits ⇐ **T ÷ r** robots on the way
**Quota = door rate × trip time**

segs.en: {An everyday example:} a metro line sends a train every **2 minutes**, and a trip takes **20 minutes**, so **20 ÷ 2 = 10 trains** are running on the line at once.
segs.zh: 生活比方：地铁每 **2 分钟**发一班，一趟全程 **20 分钟**。线路上同时跑着的车就是 **20 ÷ 2 = 10 列**。
segs.key: Everyday example: metro, a train every **2 min**, a trip **20 min** → **20 ÷ 2 = 10 trains** on the line at once

segs.en: 【指左图上半】 Fewer robots, and the door **waits**; 【指左图下半】 more, and the extras only **queue** and **block the other side**.
segs.zh: 【指左图上半】车少了，门就**等车**；【指左图下半】车多了，多出来的只会**排队**，还会**挡住对面**。
segs.key: Fewer → the door **waits** · more → extras **queue** and **block the other side**

title: Scheduling 2: when should the door switch sides?
figs: 门速度曲线（演讲专用：U(n) = nh / ((n−1)h + s)，h = 10、s = 34 用 5 局实测的中位数）；试过的换向规则对比表（幻灯片上直接画的）
hints: Tried: fixed timetable −5.0%, −6.4%; ≤ 80 steps per turn −1.1%; until empty = best
Same direction ≈ 10 ticks, after a switch ≈ 34 → 34 − 10 = 24 extra per switch
Timing histograms: backup slide 1

segs.en: {When should the door switch sides? We tried three rules:} a **fixed timetable** lost **5.0 and 6.4 percent**; **at most 80 steps** per turn lost **1.1 percent**; **serving one side until it is empty** was best.
segs.zh: 门什么时候换方向？我们试了三种规则：**按固定时间表**换，少了 **5.0% 和 6.4%**；**每轮最多放 80 步**，少了 **1.1%**；**一边走空再换**最好。
segs.key: Tried **three switching rules** (table)

segs.en: {Why?} We timed **1,255 crossings** of door 6: in the same direction, the next robot comes after about **10 ticks**; after a switch, the first one needs about **34**{, because the door and the buffer must empty first}. {So} each switch costs **34 − 10 = 24 extra ticks**.
segs.zh: 为什么？我们给门 6 的 **1255 次过门**计时：同一个方向，下一台大约隔 **10 拍**；换方向后，第一台要隔大约 **34 拍**，因为门和缓冲区要先清空。所以每换一次方向多花 **34 − 10 = 24 拍**。
segs.key: **1,255 crossings** timed: same direction **10 ticks**, after a switch **34** → each switch costs **34 − 10 = 24 extra ticks**

segs.en: 【指公式】 {So} a turn of **n** robots takes **34 + 10 × (n − 1)** ticks instead of **10 × n**. 【指曲线左端】 One robot per turn uses only **10 ÷ 34 = 29 percent** of the door's top speed; 【指 n = 10】 ten per turn, **100 ÷ (34 + 90) = 81 percent**. {Serving until empty let about 9 robots through per turn.}
segs.zh: 【指公式】所以一轮放 **n** 台要 **34 + 10 × (n − 1)** 拍，而不换向只要 **10 × n** 拍。【指曲线左端】每轮只放 1 台，门只用到最快速度的 **10 ÷ 34 = 29%**；【指 n = 10】每轮放 10 台，用到 **100 ÷ (34 + 90) = 81%**。走空再换平均每轮放大约 **9 台**。
key: Turn of **n**: **34 + 10 × (n − 1)** ticks, instead of **10 × n**
1 per turn: **10 ÷ 34 = 29%** · 10 per turn: **100 ÷ (34 + 90) = 81%** → serve **until empty**

We tried three rules:} a **fixed timetable** lost **5.0 and 6.4 percent**; **at most 80 steps** per turn lost **1.1 percent**; **serving one side until it is empty** was best. {Why?} We timed **1,255 crossings** of door 6: in the same direction, the next robot comes after about **10 ticks**; after a switch, the first one needs about **34**{, because the door and the buffer must empty first}. {So} each switch costs **34 − 10 = 24 extra ticks**. 【指公式】 {So} a turn of **n** robots takes **34 + 10 × (n − 1)** ticks instead of **10 × n**. 【指曲线左端】 One robot per turn uses only **10 ÷ 34 = 29 percent** of the door's top speed; 【指 n = 10】 ten per turn, **100 ÷ (34 + 90) = 81 percent**. {Serving until empty let about 9 robots through per turn.}

title: Scheduling 2: how big should the buffer be?
figs: 门口规则详图 B：缓冲区大小扫描（12 个开发实例；从 fig_door_rule_deck.png 切出）；试过的格数对比表（幻灯片上直接画的）
hints: Tried 1–6 cells on 12 dev instances
1, 2 cells −9.0%, −5.2% (no room to come out); 3 cells: deadlocks 11 → 29 in confirmation; 6 cells −4.2% (blocks other doors) → 4 best

Hand over to Speaker 4

segs.en: 【指上图】 {How far back should the waiting side stand?} We tried **1 to 6 cells** on **12 development instances**.
segs.zh: 【指上图】等着的一边该退后几格？我们在 **12 个开发实例**上试了 **1 到 6 格**。
segs.key: How far back should the waiting side stand? Tried **1 to 6 cells**

segs.en: 【指下方表格】 1 and 2 cells lost **9.0 and 5.2 percent**{: robots coming out had no room}. 3 cells caused more **deadlocks** {in a confirmation test}, **11 to 29** runs. 6 cells lost **4.2 percent**{: the queue blocked other doors}. **4 cells was best**.
segs.zh: 【指下方表格】1 格、2 格分别少 **9.0%、5.2%**：出门的车没地方走；3 格在确认测试里**堵死**的局从 **11 局增到 29 局**；6 格少 **4.2%**：排队的车挡住了别的门。**4 格最好**。

segs.en: {Why?} Robots come out every **9 to 10 ticks** and a move takes **3 ticks**, so they are only **10 ÷ 3 ≈ 3 cells** apart: 3 is the minimum, and one more cell leaves room for **random pauses**. {Over to Speaker 4.}
segs.zh: 为什么？门里每 **9 到 10 拍**出来一台，走一步要 **3 拍**，所以出门的车前后只隔 **10 ÷ 3 ≈ 3 格**：3 格是下限，多留 1 格给**随机暂停**留出余地。下面交给讲者 4。

**3 = minimum**, one more cell for **random pauses**

title: Lessons: why DoorFlow looks like this
figs: 五条经验卡片（幻灯片上；数字取自报告第九节）
hints: Lessons from all versions on slide 6
Door 6 cannot be bypassed: 14 of 15 rerouting lower → control how many, not where
Cannot drop, take cells → only decide who goes and when
Waiting less ≠ crossing more: credit flow −2.74% → judge by orders finished
Few maps only (7 of 69) → confirm on new maps; measure first (38 of 69 stopped before code)
en: {Looking back at slide 6,} five lessons explain **why DoorFlow looks like this**. 【指第一张卡】 Door 6 cannot be bypassed: **14 of 15** rerouting methods lowered results, so we control **how many robots go**, not where. 【指第二张卡】 Robots cannot be dropped and take up cells, so dropping or buffering methods do not carry over: we only decide **who goes and when**. 【指第三张卡】 Waiting less is not crossing more: **hop-by-hop credit flow** cut waiting but lowered results by **2.74 percent**, so we judge every change by orders finished. 【指第四张卡】 Gains on a few maps do not count: **7 of 69** ideas failed on new maps, so we confirm on new maps. 【指第五张卡】 {And} we **measure the possible gain first**: **38 of 69** ideas stopped there, before any code.
zh: 回头看第 6 页，五条经验解释了 **DoorFlow 为什么是这个样子**。【指第一张卡】门 6 绕不开：15 种换路办法里 **14 种**都变差，所以我们管**派多少车**，不管走哪条路。【指第二张卡】车不能丢、还占着格子，所以靠“丢掉”或“先存起来”的办法都用不上；我们只决定**谁走、什么时候走**。【指第三张卡】等得少不等于过得多：**逐跳信用流控**让车等得少了，结果却少了 **2.74%**，所以每项改动都按完成的单数来判断。【指第四张卡】只在少数图上有提升不算数：69 种里有 **7 种**换新图就不行，所以要换新图确认。【指第五张卡】而且**先量能省多少**：69 种里有 **38 种**量完就停了，没写代码。

segs.en: {Looking back at slide 6,} five lessons explain **why DoorFlow looks like this**.
segs.zh: 回头看第 6 页，五条经验解释了 **DoorFlow 为什么是这个样子**。

segs.en: 【指第二张卡】 Robots cannot be dropped and take up cells, so dropping or buffering methods do not carry over: we only decide **who goes and when**.
segs.zh: 【指第二张卡】车不能丢、还占着格子，所以靠“丢掉”或“先存起来”的办法都用不上；我们只决定**谁走、什么时候走**。

segs.en: 【指第三张卡】 Waiting less is not crossing more: **hop-by-hop credit flow** cut waiting but lowered results by **2.74 percent**, so we judge every change by orders finished.
